speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly where it hurts and how long you've been limping?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does he experience pain in his left hip or groin, and does the pain worsen at night or with activity? I will also examine his range of motion in both hips to check for internal rotation limitations.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have pain in your left hip or groin area, and does the pain get worse when you try to twist your leg inward? I need to check for any limited range of motion in your hips.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: The patient is in the second grade, lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco or known toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: Let me examine your hips now; please lie down and try to rotate your left leg inward and lift it. Does this movement cause pain in your hip or groin, even though your knee hurts?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent illness, rash, weight loss, change in appetite or urinary symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: I am checking for limited internal rotation and abduction of the left hip, which are classic signs of slipped capital femoral epiphysis. Does moving your left leg in this way reproduce the pain in your knee or hip?
